text:
Anya K: quick thought — should we make fallback choreography a first-class object in the rollout API/console? e.g. a named policy that can be attached to canaries/A-B tests so teams don't rewrite the chain each time
Mike L: yes. right now folks hand-roll a bunch of scripts. would love a central policy + telemetry so we can track all fallback events
Sachin: main questions: what primitives do we expose? ordered fallback list? conditional triggers? quota-aware decisions?
Julie: +1 to ordered list + conditions. I think we need 3 trigger types: health (region down), capacity (GPU util / queue length), and quality (model quality regression)
Samir: also need integration with routing rules. e.g., if canary is 5% and fallback triggers, do we move only that 5% to fallback or route new requests to fallback until canary recovers? UX needs clarity
Anya K: propose API shape sketch (pseudo):
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": {
    "name": "staged-degrade-v1",
    "steps": [
      {"target": "model_variant:small-quant", "when": "gpu_util>85 || queue_ms>200"},
      {"target": "region:secondary", "when": "region_unhealthy(primary)"},
      {"target": "model_variant:cpu-safe", "when": "timeout>3s"}
    ],
    "max_fallbacks_per_min": 20,
    "cooldown_s": 120,
    "telemetry_keys": ["fallback.trigger","fallback.path","fallback.latency_delta"]
  }
}
```
Mike L: looks good. two thoughts: (1) quota-aware: if fallback target is a shared pool we should be able to check tenant quotas before switching (2) prefer expressive predicates rather than freeform strings — safer for validation and UI
Sachin: agree. predicate DSL like `metric("gpu_util") > 0.85 && sample(30s).p95 > 200` — compiler can validate and console can show a human-readable summary
Julie: how do we represent multi-step rollback? e.g., after fallback to region B, if region A recovers we want staged return (canary -> 1/4 traffic -> 1/2 -> full) not a hard swapback
Samir: that needs a rollout policy linked to the fallback object. maybe `post_recovery_strategy: staged-reinstate(percent_steps:[25,50,100], wait_s:60)`
Anya K: UX: in console we should surface active fallback policy, current state (which step is active), recent triggers with links to the logs, and an option to override (force disable fallback) with RBAC gate
Mike L: telemetry: each fallback event should emit structured event: {service, route, original_model, fallback_target, reason_code, triggers:[...], event_ts, request_sample_link}. That makes alerts and dashboards easy
Sachin: add counters for `fallback.attempts`, `fallback.successes`, `fallback.failed_attempts` plus histogram for `latency_delta` and `qps_before_after`
Julie: guardrails: don't allow fallback to increase tail latency beyond SLO. e.g., if fallback target has slower p95, we should only route X% and then monitor. Also enforce `max_fallbacks_per_min` per customer to avoid cascading cost spikes
Samir: interesting edge: if fallback target is cheaper (quantized) we might end up routing everything there and masking a quality regression. need a quality gate: run A/B evals on a sample and if quality drops by >threshold, stop auto-fallbacks and alert humans
Anya K: decision items for eng-platform team: 1) API DSL design (predicate language) 2) fallback runtime: synchronous check vs async circuit-breaker 3) quota checks + tenant-aware routing 4) console panels + override UX 5) telemetry/events schema 6) safety nets for quality regressions
Mike L: For #2 I'd prefer event-driven circuit: runtime subscribes to metrics stream and flips a per-route state machine. avoids blocking request path and allows rate-limited transitions
Sachin: agree, state machine with explicit states: IDLE -> WARNING -> ACTIVE -> COOLDOWN -> RECOVERING. Console shows state and last transition reason
Julie: can we reuse existing rollout objects? might be simpler to attach fallback_policy_ref with a `scope: route|model|global`
Samir: implementational note: when fallback target requires different tokenization/model schema we need an adapter layer or strict compatibility checks in preflight. don't want corrupted responses in prod
Anya K: testing plan: unit tests for DSL compiler, integration tests that simulate metrics streams to trigger fallbacks, e2e in staging with canary traffic generator, and a chaos test: kill primary region and validate fallback and staged-return behaviour
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for service=prompt-router, id=cr-2026-312 (FYI) :rocket:
ops-bot: FYI — alert rule `fallback.rate_high` triggered twice on staging yesterday, linked: https://go/redwood/alerts/7981
Mike L: action items: I'll prototype predicate DSL and state machine in a branch, will open PR with API proposal by EOD Thursday. tagging @Sachin for telemetry schema and @Julie for console mockups
Sachin: will draft telemetry event schema and Prom/Hist counter names tomorrow
Julie: I'll sketch console wireframes and add an override modal with RBAC notes
Anya K: thanks — once PRs land let's do a quick sync with a live whiteboard and pick defaults for `max_fallbacks_per_min` and `cooldown_s`
Samir: and add a note in docs about compatibility checks for model variants (tokenizer/schema)
Anya K: cool. marking as next-quarter OKR candidate if we can scope an MVP (predicate DSL + state machine + basic console surface + telemetry) :thumbsup:
